comparison: Perfect match on claims C36-C41 about intrinsic model limitations. Both evaluations find these claims SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes the model correctly reproduces Tsodyks model behavior and identifies incompatibility with experimental data. Peer review praises this as part of systematic model comparison that the community needs.

Perfect match on claims C42-C46 about extrinsic model behavior. Both evaluations find these claims SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes successful reproduction of direction-independent phase precession. Peer review accepts this as established background within the systematic comparison framework.

Perfect match on claims C50-C57 about model enhancements (STF mechanism). Both evaluations find these claims SUPPORTED. OpenEval highlights quantitative improvements in precession slopes. Peer review treats these technical features as methodologically sound without raising concerns.

Perfect match on claims C77-C78 about model robustness across parameters. Both evaluations find these claims SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes core phenomena persist across parameter ranges. Peer review implicitly accepts this as supplementary evidence without raising concerns.

Perfect match on claims C96-C98 about CA3 recurrence not being strictly necessary. Both evaluations find these claims SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes model flexibility and theoretical implications. Peer review accepts this as part of systematic model analysis without criticism.

High overlap on lesion predictions (C79-C80, C84-C85). Both evaluations find these claims SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes quantitative agreement with Ahmadi et al. 2022. Peer review acknowledges connection to published/unpublished lesion work and treats predictions as supporting evidence.

Strong overlap on tempotron analysis (C101-C105). Both evaluations find these claims SUPPORTED. OpenEval provides detailed methodological assessment showing direction-invariant landmark detection. Peer review explicitly recognizes this as a core contribution demonstrating functional distinction between sequence types.

Partial overlap on hybrid model architecture (C5-C7 shared). Both evaluations find claims SUPPORTED. OpenEval focuses on model generating both sequence types with simulation evidence. Peer review emphasizes novelty of combining mechanisms and recognizes this as core contribution praised by all reviewers.

Partial overlap on DG loop mechanism (C65-C66, C71 shared). Both evaluations find claims SUPPORTED. OpenEval details how DG loops generate both sequence types simultaneously. Peer review recognizes this as part of convincing theoretical framework explaining sequence segregation.

Overlap on empirical motivation for hybrid model (C47-C49). Both evaluations find claims SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes strong experimental justification from multiple citations. Peer review treats this as foundational motivation that is central and uncontested by all reviewers.

Overlap on directional input insufficiency (C61-C62). Both evaluations find claims SUPPORTED. OpenEval shows quantitative match with experimental phase distributions while demonstrating need for DG loops. Peer review accepts this as demonstrating necessity of DG loop component central to model novelty.

Overlap on quantitative agreement with Yiu et al. 2022 (C72-C74). Both evaluations find claims SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes successful reproduction of extrinsicity/intrinsicity ratio trends. Peer review commends systematic comparison with experiments as part of convincing framework.

Overlap on 2D environment behavior (C90-C92). Both evaluations find claims SUPPORTED. OpenEval details spatial organization and testable predictions. Peer review accepts these as key mechanistic predictions distinguishing the hybrid model without raising concerns.

Partial overlap on 2D predictions (C87, C93). Both evaluations find claims SUPPORTED. OpenEval focuses on clear spatial organization of intrinsic sequence effects. Peer review connects to experimental observations of out-of-field firing from Sasaki et al. 2018.

Overlap on main conclusions (C108-C110). Both evaluations find claims SUPPORTED. OpenEval synthesizes evidence from simulations, lesions, and tempotron analysis. Peer review recognizes this as explaining sequence segregation within convincing theoretical framework.

Overlap on functional role of intrinsic sequences (C100, C106-C107). Both evaluations find claims SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes tempotron evidence for direction-invariant landmarks. Peer review highlights this novel interpretation as key contribution explicitly praised by reviewers.

Overlap on connection to Kay et al. 2020 and Sasaki et al. 2018 (C124-C125). Both evaluations find claims SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes mechanistic explanations for observed phenomena. Peer review connects predictions to experimental observations without challenge.

Overlap on remapping predictions (C130-C131). Both evaluations rate as UNCERTAIN. OpenEval acknowledges predictions are logical but lack direct empirical support and may be difficult to test. Peer review treats these as untested predictions representing future directions rather than current findings.

Overlap on broader functional roles (C156-C158). Both evaluations rate as UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes these are explicitly speculative despite theoretical citations. Peer review similarly treats these as forward-looking predictions about broader implications without explicit evaluation.

Overlap on functional roles for intrinsic sequences (C152-C153). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED based on tempotron analysis and theoretical work, though notes some aspects remain speculative. Peer review rates UNCERTAIN, treating these as untested predictions rather than demonstrated results.

OpenEval evaluates background claims C1-C4 about hippocampal place cells and 2D navigation as SUPPORTED based on established literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found - these foundational claims are not explicitly discussed in peer reviews.

OpenEval evaluates claims C114-C121 about hybrid model resolving problems with purely intrinsic models as SUPPORTED, showing reduced phase precession in reverse runs. No direct peer review match, though related to peer R8 on hybrid model necessity.

OpenEval evaluates claims C126-C129 connecting model to place field plasticity and skewness literature as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific connections to plasticity literature.

OpenEval evaluates claims C132-C138 about anatomical plausibility of DG loops as SUPPORTED through multiple citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found - anatomical feasibility not explicitly discussed by reviewers.

OpenEval rates claims C139-C140 about DG loop formation mechanisms as UNCERTAIN, acknowledging speculation despite theoretical support. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these mechanistic origin questions.

OpenEval evaluates claims C141-C147 about directional phase modulation and phase-rate relationship as SUPPORTED, reconciling conflicting findings. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific mechanistic explanations.

Peer review rates claims C10, C35, C155 about replay/preplay hypotheses as UNCERTAIN, noting these are explicitly stated as speculations by authors. OpenEval R24 partially overlaps (C155) but peer R15 includes additional claims not separately evaluated by OpenEval.
